module

public import MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Measure.RadonProduct
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Basic

/-!
# Compact-support pure products for the actual Borel Radon measure

The literal product of compact-support factor functions has compact support
on the topological product. For complex factors, its squared norm is the
literal product of the two real squared-norm functions. Coordinate integration
retains an actual compact-support function, and the original Radon-product
integral gives the exact pure-product square-integral identity.

The inputs remain arbitrary locally compact Hausdorff Borel factor spaces
and measures finite on compact sets. The completed L2 tensor identification
and its dense extension remain separate obligations.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped CompactlySupported

noncomputable section

universe uX uY uR

namespace CompactlySupportedContinuousMap

section Product

variable {X : Type uX} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X]
variable {Y : Type uY} [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y]
variable {R : Type uR} [TopologicalSpace R] [MulZeroClass R] [ContinuousMul R]

/-- The literal pure product of compact-support functions on the original topological product. -/
def mulProd (f : C_c(X, R)) (g : C_c(Y, R)) : C_c(X × Y, R) where
  toFun z := f z.1 * g z.2
  continuous_toFun := (f.continuous.comp continuous_fst).mul (g.continuous.comp continuous_snd)
  hasCompactSupport' := by
    apply HasCompactSupport.intro (f.hasCompactSupport.prod g.hasCompactSupport)
    rintro ⟨x, y⟩ hxy
    by_cases hx : x ∈ tsupport f
    · have hy : y ∉ tsupport g := fun hy => hxy ⟨hx, hy⟩
      simp only [image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport hy, mul_zero]
    · simp only [image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport hx, zero_mul]

/-- The compact-support pure product has its exact original factor values. -/
@[simp]
theorem mulProd_apply (f : C_c(X, R)) (g : C_c(Y, R)) (x : X) (y : Y) :
    mulProd f g (x, y) = f x * g y := rfl

end Product

section NormSquare

variable {X : Type uX} [TopologicalSpace X]

/-- The actual real squared-norm function of a complex compact-support function. -/
def normSq (f : C_c(X, ℂ)) : C_c(X, ℝ) where
  toFun x := ‖f x‖ ^ 2
  continuous_toFun := f.continuous.norm.pow 2
  hasCompactSupport' := f.hasCompactSupport.comp_left (g := fun z : ℂ => ‖z‖ ^ 2) (by simp)

/-- The compact-support squared norm has the literal real squared-norm values. -/
@[simp]
theorem normSq_apply (f : C_c(X, ℂ)) (x : X) : normSq f x = ‖f x‖ ^ 2 := rfl

variable [T2Space X]
variable {Y : Type uY} [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y]

/-- The pure complex product's squared norm is the actual product of the factor squared norms. -/
theorem normSq_mulProd (f : C_c(X, ℂ)) (g : C_c(Y, ℂ)) :
    normSq (mulProd f g) = mulProd (normSq f) (normSq g) := by
  ext z
  rcases z with ⟨x, y⟩
  simp only [normSq_apply, mulProd_apply, norm_mul, mul_pow]

end NormSquare

section CoordinateIntegral

variable {X : Type uX} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X]
variable {Y : Type uY} [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y]
  [MeasurableSpace Y] [OpensMeasurableSpace Y]
variable (ν : Measure Y) [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts ν]

/-- The real pure product's coordinate integral is the original factor times the actual scalar integral. -/
theorem integralRight_mulProd (f : C_c(X, ℝ)) (g : C_c(Y, ℝ)) :
    integralRight ν (mulProd f g) = (∫ y : Y, g y ∂ν) • f := by
  ext x
  change (∫ y : Y, f x * g y ∂ν) = (∫ y : Y, g y ∂ν) * f x
  rw [integral_const_mul]
  exact mul_comm _ _

/-- Coordinate integration of the pure square retains the actual compact-support squared-norm factor. -/
theorem integralRight_normSq_mulProd (f : C_c(X, ℂ)) (g : C_c(Y, ℂ)) :
    integralRight ν (normSq (mulProd f g)) = (∫ y : Y, ‖g y‖ ^ 2 ∂ν) • normSq f := by
  rw [normSq_mulProd]
  exact integralRight_mulProd ν (normSq f) (normSq g)

end CoordinateIntegral

end CompactlySupportedContinuousMap

namespace MeasureTheory.Measure

open CompactlySupportedContinuousMap

variable {X : Type uX} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X]
  [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]
variable {Y : Type uY} [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y] [LocallyCompactSpace Y]
  [MeasurableSpace Y] [BorelSpace Y]
variable (μ : Measure X) (ν : Measure Y)
  [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ] [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts ν]

/-- The Borel measurable space of the literal product used for compact-support Radon integration. -/
local instance instCompactSupportProductBorelMeasurableSpace : MeasurableSpace (X × Y) := borel (X × Y)
local instance instCompactSupportProductBorelSpace : BorelSpace (X × Y) := ⟨rfl⟩

/-- The actual Borel Radon integral of a real compact-support pure product factors exactly. -/
theorem integral_mulProd (f : C_c(X, ℝ)) (g : C_c(Y, ℝ)) :
    ∫ z : X × Y, mulProd f g z ∂(radonProd μ ν) =
      (∫ x : X, f x ∂μ) * ∫ y : Y, g y ∂ν := by
  calc
    ∫ z : X × Y, mulProd f g z ∂(radonProd μ ν) =
        ∫ x : X, ∫ y : Y, f x * g y ∂ν ∂μ := integral_radonProd μ ν (mulProd f g)
    _ = ∫ x : X, f x * (∫ y : Y, g y ∂ν) ∂μ :=
      integral_congr_ae (Eventually.of_forall fun x => integral_const_mul (f x) (g : Y → ℝ))
    _ = (∫ x : X, f x ∂μ) * ∫ y : Y, g y ∂ν :=
      integral_mul_const (∫ y : Y, g y ∂ν) (f : X → ℝ)

/-- The pure complex product has the exact original product of square integrals on the Borel Radon carrier. -/
theorem integral_norm_sq_mulProd (f : C_c(X, ℂ)) (g : C_c(Y, ℂ)) :
    ∫ z : X × Y, ‖mulProd f g z‖ ^ 2 ∂(radonProd μ ν) =
      (∫ x : X, ‖f x‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) * ∫ y : Y, ‖g y‖ ^ 2 ∂ν := by
  change (∫ z : X × Y, normSq (mulProd f g) z ∂(radonProd μ ν)) = _
  rw [normSq_mulProd]
  exact integral_mulProd μ ν (normSq f) (normSq g)

end MeasureTheory.Measure

end

module

public import MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Measure.RadonProduct
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Prod

/-!
# Reverse compact-support integration for the actual Borel Radon product

The published compact-support Fubini theorem applies to the original
jointly continuous real function and the two factor measures finite on
compact sets. Together with the defining Radon-product integral, it gives
the original reverse-order formula on the topological product.

There is no global s-finiteness or countability assumption, and no equality
between the product Borel sigma-algebra and the factor product sigma-algebra.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open MeasureTheory
open scoped CompactlySupported

namespace MeasureTheory.Measure

universe uX uY

variable {X : Type uX} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X]
  [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]
variable {Y : Type uY} [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y] [LocallyCompactSpace Y]
  [MeasurableSpace Y] [BorelSpace Y]
variable (μ : Measure X) (ν : Measure Y)
  [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ] [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts ν]

/-- The actual Borel measurable space of the topological product. -/
local instance instFubiniProductMeasurableSpace : MeasurableSpace (X × Y) := borel (X × Y)
local instance instFubiniProductBorelSpace : BorelSpace (X × Y) := ⟨rfl⟩

omit [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X] [T2Space Y] [LocallyCompactSpace Y] in
/-- The original real compact-support coordinate integrals have equal values in both orders. -/
theorem integral_integral_radonProd_swap (f : C_c(X × Y, ℝ)) :
    (∫ x : X, ∫ y : Y, f (x, y) ∂ν ∂μ) =
      ∫ y : Y, ∫ x : X, f (x, y) ∂μ ∂ν := by
  have huncurry : Function.uncurry (fun (x : X) (y : Y) => f (x, y)) =
      (f : X × Y → ℝ) := by
    funext z
    rcases z with ⟨x, y⟩
    rfl
  exact integral_integral_swap_of_hasCompactSupport
    (huncurry.symm ▸ f.continuous) (huncurry.symm ▸ f.hasCompactSupport)

/-- The actual Borel Radon-product integral has the original reverse-coordinate formula. -/
theorem integral_radonProd_swap (f : C_c(X × Y, ℝ)) :
    (∫ z : X × Y, f z ∂(radonProd μ ν)) =
      ∫ y : Y, ∫ x : X, f (x, y) ∂μ ∂ν := by
  rw [integral_radonProd μ ν f]
  exact integral_integral_radonProd_swap μ ν f

end MeasureTheory.Measure

module

public import MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Measure.RadonProduct.CompactSupport
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Group.Integral
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.Basic
public import Mathlib.Topology.UrysohnsLemma

/-!
# Haar invariance of the actual Borel Radon product

The compact-support integral formula and the original coordinate Haar
invariance prove invariance under actual product left translation. Positive
compact-support factor integrals prove that the constructed product is
nonzero. Its existing regularity then supplies open positivity, giving a
genuine Haar measure on the Borel sigma-algebra of the topological product.

No countability, s-finiteness or product-sigma-algebra identification is
used. The variable-coordinate shear and reverse-order compact-support
Fubini theorem remain separate obligations.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped CompactlySupported

namespace MeasureTheory.Measure

noncomputable section

universe uG uK

variable {G : Type uG} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
  [T2Space G] [LocallyCompactSpace G] [MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G]
variable {K : Type uK} [Group K] [TopologicalSpace K] [IsTopologicalGroup K]
  [T2Space K] [LocallyCompactSpace K] [MeasurableSpace K] [BorelSpace K]
variable (μ : Measure G) (ν : Measure K) [μ.Regular] [ν.Regular]

/-- The literal Borel measurable space of the topological product. -/
local instance instHaarRadonProductMeasurableSpace : MeasurableSpace (G × K) := borel (G × K)
local instance instHaarRadonProductBorelSpace : BorelSpace (G × K) := ⟨rfl⟩

section Invariance

variable [IsMulLeftInvariant μ] [IsMulLeftInvariant ν]

/-- Actual left translation in both coordinates preserves the original Borel Radon product. -/
theorem map_mulLeft_radonProd (a : G × K) :
    Measure.map (a * ·) (radonProd μ ν) = radonProd μ ν := by
  let e : (G × K) ≃ₜ (G × K) := Homeomorph.mulLeft a
  change Measure.map e (radonProd μ ν) = radonProd μ ν
  let : (Measure.map e (radonProd μ ν)).Regular := Measure.Regular.map e
  apply Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported
  intro f
  rw [e.measurableEmbedding.integral_map]
  let f' : C_c(G × K, ℝ) :=
    ⟨⟨fun z => f (e z), f.continuous.comp e.continuous⟩,
      f.hasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph e⟩
  change (∫ z : G × K, f' z ∂(radonProd μ ν)) =
    ∫ z : G × K, f z ∂(radonProd μ ν)
  rw [integral_radonProd μ ν f', integral_radonProd μ ν f]
  change (∫ s : G, ∫ t : K, f (a.1 * s, a.2 * t) ∂ν ∂μ) =
    ∫ s : G, ∫ t : K, f (s, t) ∂ν ∂μ
  calc
    (∫ s : G, ∫ t : K, f (a.1 * s, a.2 * t) ∂ν ∂μ) =
        ∫ s : G, ∫ t : K, f (a.1 * s, t) ∂ν ∂μ := by
      apply integral_congr_ae
      exact Eventually.of_forall fun s =>
        integral_mul_left_eq_self (μ := ν) (fun t : K => f (a.1 * s, t)) a.2
    _ = ∫ s : G, ∫ t : K, f (s, t) ∂ν ∂μ :=
      integral_mul_left_eq_self (μ := μ) (fun s : G => ∫ t : K, f (s, t) ∂ν) a.1

/-- The original Radon product is left invariant for the literal product group. -/
instance isMulLeftInvariant_radonProd : IsMulLeftInvariant (radonProd μ ν) where
  map_mul_left_eq_self := map_mulLeft_radonProd μ ν

/-- The actual product left translation is measure preserving on the full Borel carrier. -/
theorem measurePreserving_mulLeft_radonProd (a : G × K) :
    MeasurePreserving (a * ·) (radonProd μ ν) (radonProd μ ν) :=
  ⟨(Homeomorph.mulLeft a).measurable, map_mulLeft_radonProd μ ν a⟩

end Invariance

section Nonzero

variable [μ.IsHaarMeasure] [ν.IsHaarMeasure]

private theorem exists_compactSupport_integral_pos
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X]
    [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]
    (η : Measure X) [η.Regular] [η.IsOpenPosMeasure] (x : X) :
    ∃ f : C_c(X, ℝ), 0 < ∫ z : X, f z ∂η := by
  obtain ⟨f, hfCompact, hfNonneg, hfx⟩ := exists_continuous_nonneg_pos x
  let F : C_c(X, ℝ) := ⟨f, hfCompact⟩
  exact ⟨F, integral_pos_of_integrable_nonneg_nonzero f.continuous F.integrable hfNonneg hfx⟩

omit [IsTopologicalGroup G] [IsTopologicalGroup K] in
/-- Positive original factor integrals make the actual Radon product nonzero. -/
theorem radonProd_ne_zero : radonProd μ ν ≠ 0 := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := exists_compactSupport_integral_pos μ (1 : G)
  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := exists_compactSupport_integral_pos ν (1 : K)
  have hpos : 0 < ∫ z : G × K, CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.mulProd f g z ∂(radonProd μ ν) := by
    rw [integral_mulProd μ ν f g]
    exact mul_pos hf hg
  intro hzero
  rw [hzero] at hpos
  simp only [integral_zero_measure] at hpos
  exact (lt_irrefl (0 : ℝ)) hpos

/-- The constructed Borel Radon product of the original regular Haar measures is a Haar measure. -/
instance isHaarMeasure_radonProd : (radonProd μ ν).IsHaarMeasure := by
  let : NeZero (radonProd μ ν) := ⟨radonProd_ne_zero μ ν⟩
  exact
    { toIsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts := inferInstance
      toIsMulLeftInvariant := inferInstance
      toIsOpenPosMeasure := inferInstance }

end Nonzero

end

end MeasureTheory.Measure

module

public import MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Measure.RadonProduct.Fubini

/-!
# Coordinate exchange of the actual Borel Radon product

Compact-support integral uniqueness and the original reverse Fubini law
prove the literal exchange of two topological Borel Radon measures.
Independent factors and zero measures remain; no L2 or Haar model enters.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open MeasureTheory
open scoped CompactlySupported

namespace MeasureTheory.Measure

universe uX uY

variable {X : Type uX} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X]
  [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]
variable {Y : Type uY} [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y] [LocallyCompactSpace Y]
  [MeasurableSpace Y] [BorelSpace Y]
variable (μ : Measure X) (ν : Measure Y)
  [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ] [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts ν]

/-- The original Borel measurable structure of the X-first topological product. -/
local instance instSwapXYMeasurableSpace : MeasurableSpace (X × Y) := borel (X × Y)
local instance instSwapXYBorelSpace : BorelSpace (X × Y) := ⟨rfl⟩

/-- The original Borel measurable structure of the Y-first topological product. -/
local instance instSwapYXMeasurableSpace : MeasurableSpace (Y × X) := borel (Y × X)
local instance instSwapYXBorelSpace : BorelSpace (Y × X) := ⟨rfl⟩

/-- Literal coordinate exchange maps the actual Borel Radon product to its reversed product. -/
theorem map_prodSwap_radonProd :
    Measure.map (Prod.swap : X × Y → Y × X) (radonProd μ ν) = radonProd ν μ := by
  let e := Homeomorph.prodComm X Y
  change Measure.map e (radonProd μ ν) = radonProd ν μ
  let _ : (Measure.map e (radonProd μ ν)).Regular := Measure.Regular.map e
  apply Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported
  intro f
  rw [e.measurableEmbedding.integral_map]
  let F : C_c(X × Y, ℝ) :=
    ⟨⟨fun z => f (e z), f.continuous.comp e.continuous⟩,
      f.hasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph e⟩
  change (∫ z : X × Y, F z ∂(radonProd μ ν)) = ∫ z : Y × X, f z ∂(radonProd ν μ)
  rw [integral_radonProd μ ν F, integral_radonProd_swap ν μ f]
  rfl

/-- Coordinate exchange preserves the actual two Borel Radon measures in their original orders. -/
theorem measurePreserving_prodSwap_radonProd :
    MeasurePreserving (Prod.swap : X × Y → Y × X) (radonProd μ ν) (radonProd ν μ) :=
  ⟨(Homeomorph.prodComm X Y).measurable, map_prodSwap_radonProd μ ν⟩


end MeasureTheory.Measure

module

public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Regular

/-!
# Regularity of finite measures under domination

A measure dominated by a finite regular Borel measure is regular.  The proof
uses compact approximation for the upper measure and therefore needs no
metrizability or countability assumption.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Set
open scoped ENNReal NNReal

namespace MeasureTheory.Measure.Regular

universe u

variable {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [R1Space X]
  [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]

/-- A measure dominated by a finite regular measure is regular.  This applies
on nonmetrizable compact Hausdorff Borel spaces as well as metric spaces. -/
theorem of_le {nu mu : Measure X} [mu.Regular] [IsFiniteMeasure mu]
    (h : nu ≤ mu) : nu.Regular := by
  let : IsFiniteMeasure nu := isFiniteMeasure_of_le mu h
  let : InnerRegularCompactLTTop nu := by
    refine ⟨?_⟩
    intro A hA r hr
    have heps : nu A - r ≠ 0 := (tsub_pos_of_lt hr).ne'
    obtain ⟨K, hKA, hKcompact, _hKclosed, hmuK⟩ :=
      hA.1.exists_isCompact_isClosed_sdiff_lt (measure_ne_top mu A) heps
    refine ⟨K, hKA, hKcompact, ?_⟩
    have hnuK : nu (A \ K) < nu A - r :=
      (h (A \ K)).trans_lt hmuK
    have hdiff : nu A - nu K < nu A - r :=
      le_measure_sdiff.trans_lt hnuK
    exact lt_of_tsub_lt_tsub_left hdiff
  infer_instance

/-- The sum of two finite regular measures is regular. -/
theorem add_of_finite (mu nu : Measure X) [mu.Regular] [nu.Regular]
    [IsFiniteMeasure mu] [IsFiniteMeasure nu] : (mu + nu).Regular := by
  infer_instance

/-- A measure dominated by a finite nonnegative scalar multiple of a finite
regular measure is regular. -/
theorem of_le_nnreal_smul {nu mu : Measure X} [mu.Regular] [IsFiniteMeasure mu]
    (c : ℝ≥0) (h : nu ≤ c • mu) : nu.Regular := by
  let : (c • mu).Regular := by infer_instance
  let : IsFiniteMeasure (c • mu) := by infer_instance
  exact of_le h

end MeasureTheory.Measure.Regular

-/
module

public import MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.RegularVariation
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntegrableOn
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.Integral
public import Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousMap.Compact

/-!
# Regular signed measures and integration on continuous functions

This file packages the real signed measures whose total variation is regular as
a real submodule.  On a compact Borel space, integration against such a measure
is a bounded real functional on the continuous real-valued functions.  The
construction installs no regularity or norm instance on the ambient type of
signed measures.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped ENNReal NNReal

namespace MathlibExt.MeasureTheory

noncomputable section

universe u

variable {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [R1Space X]
  [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]

/-- Signed measures with regular total variation, as a real submodule of all
signed measures. -/
noncomputable def regularSignedMeasureSubmodule (X : Type u)
    [TopologicalSpace X] [R1Space X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] :
    Submodule ℝ (SignedMeasure X) where
  carrier := {s | s.totalVariation.Regular}
  zero_mem' :=
    (SignedMeasure.totalVariation_regular_iff_hasRegularVariation
      (0 : SignedMeasure X)).2 VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation.zero
  add_mem' := by
    intro s t hs ht
    apply (SignedMeasure.totalVariation_regular_iff_hasRegularVariation (s + t)).2
    let _ : IsFiniteMeasure s.variation := by
      rw [← SignedMeasure.totalVariation_eq_variation]
      infer_instance
    let _ : IsFiniteMeasure t.variation := by
      rw [← SignedMeasure.totalVariation_eq_variation]
      infer_instance
    exact ((SignedMeasure.totalVariation_regular_iff_hasRegularVariation s).1 hs).add
      ((SignedMeasure.totalVariation_regular_iff_hasRegularVariation t).1 ht)
  smul_mem' := by
    intro c s hs
    exact (SignedMeasure.totalVariation_regular_iff_hasRegularVariation (c • s)).2
      (((SignedMeasure.totalVariation_regular_iff_hasRegularVariation s).1 hs).smul c)

/-- A real signed measure whose total variation is regular. -/
abbrev RegularSignedMeasure (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] [R1Space X]
    [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] :=
  ↑(regularSignedMeasureSubmodule X)

namespace RegularSignedMeasure

/-- The defining regularity property of a regular signed measure. -/
theorem totalVariation_regular (s : RegularSignedMeasure X) :
    (s : SignedMeasure X).totalVariation.Regular :=
  s.property

/-- A regular signed measure has regular variation in the generic vector-measure sense. -/
theorem hasRegularVariation (s : RegularSignedMeasure X) :
    VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation (s : SignedMeasure X) :=
  (SignedMeasure.totalVariation_regular_iff_hasRegularVariation (s : SignedMeasure X)).1
    s.property

omit [TopologicalSpace X] [R1Space X] [BorelSpace X] in
private theorem variationFinite (s : SignedMeasure X) :
    IsFiniteMeasure s.variation := by
  rw [← SignedMeasure.totalVariation_eq_variation]
  infer_instance

variable [CompactSpace X]

omit [R1Space X] in
private theorem continuousMap_integrable (s : SignedMeasure X) (f : C(X, ℝ)) :
    s.Integrable fun x ↦ f x := by
  let _ : IsFiniteMeasure s.variation := variationFinite s
  apply Integrable.of_bound f.continuous.measurable.aestronglyMeasurable ‖f‖
  exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x ↦ f.norm_coe_le_norm x

private noncomputable def signedIntegralLinear (s : RegularSignedMeasure X) :
    C(X, ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ where
  toFun f := ∫ᵛ x, f x ∂<•(s : SignedMeasure X)
  map_add' f g := by
    simpa only [ContinuousMap.add_apply] using
      (VectorMeasure.integral_fun_add
        (B := (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ).flip)
        (continuousMap_integrable (s : SignedMeasure X) f)
        (continuousMap_integrable (s : SignedMeasure X) g))
  map_smul' c f := by
    simpa only [ContinuousMap.smul_apply, RingHom.id_apply] using
      (VectorMeasure.integral_fun_smul (s : SignedMeasure X)
        (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ).flip c (fun x ↦ f x))

@[simp]
private theorem signedIntegralLinear_apply (s : RegularSignedMeasure X) (f : C(X, ℝ)) :
    signedIntegralLinear s f = ∫ᵛ x, f x ∂<•(s : SignedMeasure X) :=
  rfl

private theorem norm_signedIntegralLinear_apply_le
    (s : RegularSignedMeasure X) (f : C(X, ℝ)) :
    ‖signedIntegralLinear s f‖ ≤
      (s : SignedMeasure X).totalVariation.real univ * ‖f‖ := by
  let _ : IsFiniteMeasure (s : SignedMeasure X).variation :=
    variationFinite (s : SignedMeasure X)
  have h := VectorMeasure.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const
    (μ := (s : SignedMeasure X))
    (B := (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ).flip)
    (f := fun x ↦ f x)
    (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x ↦ f.norm_coe_le_norm x)
  simpa [signedIntegralLinear, SignedMeasure.totalVariation_eq_variation,
    mul_comm] using h

/-- Integration against a regular signed measure, as a bounded functional on
the continuous real-valued functions. -/
@[no_expose]
noncomputable def signedIntegralDual (s : RegularSignedMeasure X) :
    StrongDual ℝ C(X, ℝ) :=
  LinearMap.mkContinuous (signedIntegralLinear s)
    ((s : SignedMeasure X).totalVariation.real univ)
    (norm_signedIntegralLinear_apply_le s)

@[simp]
theorem signedIntegralDual_apply (s : RegularSignedMeasure X) (f : C(X, ℝ)) :
    signedIntegralDual s f = ∫ᵛ x, f x ∂<•(s : SignedMeasure X) :=
  by
    simp only [signedIntegralDual, LinearMap.mkContinuous_apply,
      signedIntegralLinear_apply]

/-- The pointwise total-variation bound for signed integration. -/
theorem norm_signedIntegralDual_apply_le
    (s : RegularSignedMeasure X) (f : C(X, ℝ)) :
    ‖signedIntegralDual s f‖ ≤
      (s : SignedMeasure X).totalVariation.real univ * ‖f‖ :=
  by
    simpa only [signedIntegralDual, LinearMap.mkContinuous_apply] using
      norm_signedIntegralLinear_apply_le s f

/-- The operator norm of signed integration is bounded by the total mass of
the total variation. -/
theorem norm_signedIntegralDual_le (s : RegularSignedMeasure X) :
    ‖signedIntegralDual s‖ ≤ (s : SignedMeasure X).totalVariation.real univ := by
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ measureReal_nonneg
  exact norm_signedIntegralDual_apply_le s

/-- Integration is real-linear in a regular signed measure. -/
@[no_expose]
noncomputable def regularSignedMeasureIntegral :
    RegularSignedMeasure X →ₗ[ℝ] StrongDual ℝ C(X, ℝ) where
  toFun := signedIntegralDual
  map_add' s t := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro f
    simp only [signedIntegralDual_apply, add_apply]
    change (∫ᵛ x, f x ∂<•((s : SignedMeasure X) + (t : SignedMeasure X))) =
      (∫ᵛ x, f x ∂<•(s : SignedMeasure X)) +
        ∫ᵛ x, f x ∂<•(t : SignedMeasure X)
    exact VectorMeasure.integral_add_vectorMeasure
      (continuousMap_integrable (s : SignedMeasure X) f)
      (continuousMap_integrable (t : SignedMeasure X) f)
  map_smul' c s := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro f
    simp only [signedIntegralDual_apply, smul_apply, RingHom.id_apply]
    change (∫ᵛ x, f x ∂<•(c • (s : SignedMeasure X))) =
      c • ∫ᵛ x, f x ∂<•(s : SignedMeasure X)
    exact VectorMeasure.integral_smul_vectorMeasure (fun x ↦ f x) c

@[simp]
theorem signedIntegralDual_zero :
    signedIntegralDual (0 : RegularSignedMeasure X) = 0 :=
  (regularSignedMeasureIntegral (X := X)).map_zero

@[simp]
theorem signedIntegralDual_add (s t : RegularSignedMeasure X) :
    signedIntegralDual (s + t) = signedIntegralDual s + signedIntegralDual t :=
  (regularSignedMeasureIntegral (X := X)).map_add s t

@[simp]
theorem signedIntegralDual_smul (c : ℝ) (s : RegularSignedMeasure X) :
    signedIntegralDual (c • s) = c • signedIntegralDual s :=
  (regularSignedMeasureIntegral (X := X)).map_smul c s

@[simp]
theorem signedIntegralDual_neg (s : RegularSignedMeasure X) :
    signedIntegralDual (-s) = -signedIntegralDual s :=
  (regularSignedMeasureIntegral (X := X)).map_neg s

@[simp]
theorem signedIntegralDual_sub (s t : RegularSignedMeasure X) :
    signedIntegralDual (s - t) = signedIntegralDual s - signedIntegralDual t :=
  (regularSignedMeasureIntegral (X := X)).map_sub s t

@[simp]
theorem regularSignedMeasureIntegral_apply
    (s : RegularSignedMeasure X) (f : C(X, ℝ)) :
    regularSignedMeasureIntegral s f =
      ∫ᵛ x, f x ∂<•(s : SignedMeasure X) :=
  signedIntegralDual_apply s f

end RegularSignedMeasure

end

module

public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.SetIntegral
public import MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function.BoundedMeasurable
public import MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.RegularVariation

import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntegrableOn

/-!
# Integrating bounded measurable functions against complex measures

This file defines the pairing of a bounded measurable complex-valued function with a complex
measure.  Every complex measure has finite total variation; the definition uses Mathlib's
vector-measure integral with complex multiplication regarded as a continuous real-bilinear map.

Although the underlying vector integral is only real-bilinear in general, complex multiplication
makes this pairing complex-linear in both the function and the measure.  The corresponding
complex-linearity results are proved explicitly below.
-/

@[expose] public section

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped ENNReal NNReal

open MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Function

namespace MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure

noncomputable section

universe u

variable {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X]

local instance complexIntegralVariationFinite (μ : ComplexMeasure X) :
    IsFiniteMeasure μ.variation :=
  ComplexMeasure.isFiniteMeasure_variation μ

/-- The integral of a bounded measurable function against a complex measure, using complex
multiplication as the real-bilinear pairing in Mathlib's vector-measure integral. -/
noncomputable def complexIntegral (μ : ComplexMeasure X) (φ : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) : ℂ :=
  ∫ᵛ x, φ x ∂[ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℂ; μ]

/-- A bounded measurable function is integrable with respect to every complex measure. -/
theorem complexIntegral_integrable (μ : ComplexMeasure X) (φ : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) :
    μ.Integrable (fun x ↦ φ x) := by
  apply Integrable.of_bound φ.measurable.aestronglyMeasurable ‖φ‖
  exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x ↦ φ.norm_apply_le_norm x

@[simp]
theorem complexIntegral_zero (μ : ComplexMeasure X) :
    complexIntegral μ (0 : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) = 0 := by
  simp [complexIntegral]

@[simp]
theorem complexIntegral_zero_measure (φ : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) :
    complexIntegral (0 : ComplexMeasure X) φ = 0 := by
  simp [complexIntegral]

/-- Additivity in the bounded measurable function. -/
theorem complexIntegral_add (μ : ComplexMeasure X) (φ ψ : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) :
    complexIntegral μ (φ + ψ) = complexIntegral μ φ + complexIntegral μ ψ := by
  change (∫ᵛ x, φ x + ψ x ∂[ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℂ; μ]) = _
  exact MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.integral_fun_add
    (complexIntegral_integrable μ φ) (complexIntegral_integrable μ ψ)

/-- Complex homogeneity in the bounded measurable function.  This uses the generic scalar
linearity theorem for `setToFun`, together with complex-linearity of multiplication in its first
argument; it does not identify complex scalar multiplication with the real scalar API of the
vector integral. -/
theorem complexIntegral_smul (μ : ComplexMeasure X) (c : ℂ)
    (φ : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) :
    complexIntegral μ (c • φ) = c • complexIntegral μ φ := by
  let B : ℂ →L[ℝ] ℂ →L[ℝ] ℂ := ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℂ
  change (∫ᵛ x, c • φ x ∂[B; μ]) = c • ∫ᵛ x, φ x ∂[B; μ]
  rw [MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.integral_eq_setToFun,
    MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.integral_eq_setToFun]
  have hline : ∀ d : ℂ, ∀ s z, μ.transpose B s (d • z) = d • μ.transpose B s z := by
    intro d s z
    change (d * z) * μ s = d * (z * μ s)
    rw [mul_assoc]
  convert (setToFun_smul (α := X) (E := ℂ) (F := ℂ) (𝕜 := ℂ)
      (μ := μ.variation) (T := μ.transpose B)
      (dominatedFinMeasAdditive_cbmApplyMeasure μ B) hline c (fun x ↦ φ x)) using 1

/-- Additivity in the complex measure. -/
theorem complexIntegral_add_measure (μ ν : ComplexMeasure X)
    (φ : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) :
    complexIntegral (μ + ν) φ = complexIntegral μ φ + complexIntegral ν φ := by
  exact MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.integral_add_vectorMeasure
    (complexIntegral_integrable μ φ) (complexIntegral_integrable ν φ)

/-- Multiplying the set-function in a `setToFun` construction by a complex scalar multiplies its
value by the same scalar.  Mathlib provides this directly for real scalars; this local lemma records
the complex consequence needed for complex measures. -/
private theorem setToFun_complex_smul_left
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    {ρ : Measure X} {T : Set X → E →L[ℝ] ℂ} {C : ℝ}
    (hT : DominatedFinMeasAdditive ρ T C) (c : ℂ) (f : X → E) :
    setToFun ρ (fun s ↦ c • T s) (hT.smul c) f = c • setToFun ρ T hT f := by
  by_cases hf : Integrable f ρ
  · apply hf.induction (P := fun g ↦
        setToFun ρ (fun s ↦ c • T s) (hT.smul c) g = c • setToFun ρ T hT g)
    · intro d s hs hρs
      rw [setToFun_indicator_const (hT.smul c) hs hρs.ne,
        setToFun_indicator_const hT hs hρs.ne]
      rfl
    · intro g h _ hgi hhi hg hh
      rw [setToFun_add (hT.smul c) hgi hhi, setToFun_add hT hgi hhi, hg, hh, smul_add]
    · exact isClosed_eq (continuous_setToFun (hT.smul c))
        ((continuous_const_smul c).comp (continuous_setToFun hT))
    · intro g h hgh _ hg
      calc
        setToFun ρ (fun s ↦ c • T s) (hT.smul c) h =
            setToFun ρ (fun s ↦ c • T s) (hT.smul c) g :=
          (setToFun_congr_ae (hT.smul c) hgh).symm
        _ = c • setToFun ρ T hT g := hg
        _ = c • setToFun ρ T hT h :=
          congrArg (c • ·) (setToFun_congr_ae hT hgh)
  · rw [setToFun_undef (hT.smul c) hf, setToFun_undef hT hf, smul_zero]

/-- Complex homogeneity in the measure.  The proof uses
`variation (c • μ) = ‖c‖₊ • variation μ` to change the reference measure, then applies the local
complex scalar extension lemma to the transposed set-function. -/
theorem complexIntegral_smul_measure (c : ℂ) (μ : ComplexMeasure X)
    (φ : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) :
    complexIntegral (c • μ) φ = c • complexIntegral μ φ := by
  let B : ℂ →L[ℝ] ℂ →L[ℝ] ℂ := ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℂ
  let T : Set X → ℂ →L[ℝ] ℂ := μ.transpose B
  let T' : Set X → ℂ →L[ℝ] ℂ := fun s ↦ c • T s
  let hT : DominatedFinMeasAdditive μ.variation T ‖B‖ :=
    dominatedFinMeasAdditive_cbmApplyMeasure μ B
  let hT' : DominatedFinMeasAdditive μ.variation T' (‖c‖ * ‖B‖) := hT.smul c
  have htranspose :
      ((c • μ).transpose B : Set X → ℂ →L[ℝ] ℂ) = T' := by
    funext s
    ext z
    change z * (c * μ s) = c * (z * μ s)
    rw [← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, mul_comm z c]
  have hT'_smul :
      DominatedFinMeasAdditive (‖c‖₊ • μ.variation) T' ‖B‖ := by
    rw [← MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.variation_smul]
    rw [← htranspose]
    exact dominatedFinMeasAdditive_cbmApplyMeasure (c • μ) B
  have hT'_c : DominatedFinMeasAdditive (c • μ).variation T' ‖B‖ := by
    rw [← htranspose]
    exact dominatedFinMeasAdditive_cbmApplyMeasure (c • μ) B
  have hvariation₁ : (c • μ).variation ≤ (1 : ℝ≥0∞) • (‖c‖₊ • μ.variation) := by
    simpa only [one_smul, MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.variation_smul] using
      (le_rfl : ‖c‖₊ • μ.variation ≤ ‖c‖₊ • μ.variation)
  have hvariation₂ : ‖c‖₊ • μ.variation ≤ (1 : ℝ≥0∞) • (c • μ).variation := by
    simpa only [one_smul, MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.variation_smul] using
      (le_rfl : ‖c‖₊ • μ.variation ≤ ‖c‖₊ • μ.variation)
  unfold complexIntegral
  rw [MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.integral_eq_setToFun,
    MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.integral_eq_setToFun]
  calc
    setToFun (c • μ).variation ((c • μ).transpose B)
        (dominatedFinMeasAdditive_cbmApplyMeasure (c • μ) B) (fun x ↦ φ x) =
        setToFun (c • μ).variation T' hT'_c (fun x ↦ φ x) := by
      apply setToFun_congr_left
      exact htranspose
    _ = setToFun (‖c‖₊ • μ.variation) T' hT'_smul (fun x ↦ φ x) :=
      setToFun_congr_measure 1 1 (by simp) (by simp) hvariation₁ hvariation₂
        hT'_c hT'_smul (fun x ↦ φ x)
    _ = setToFun μ.variation T' hT' (fun x ↦ φ x) :=
      (setToFun_congr_smul_measure' ‖c‖₊ hT' hT'_smul (fun x ↦ φ x)).symm
    _ = c • setToFun μ.variation T hT (fun x ↦ φ x) :=
      setToFun_complex_smul_left hT c (fun x ↦ φ x)
    _ = c • setToFun μ.variation (μ.transpose B)
        (dominatedFinMeasAdditive_cbmApplyMeasure μ B) (fun x ↦ φ x) := rfl

/-- The sharp total-variation bound for the complex integral pairing. -/
theorem norm_complexIntegral_le (μ : ComplexMeasure X) (φ : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) :
    ‖complexIntegral μ φ‖ ≤ ‖φ‖ * μ.variation.real univ := by
  simpa [complexIntegral, ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_mul] using
    (MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const
      (μ := μ) (B := ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℂ)
      (f := fun x ↦ φ x)
      (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x ↦ φ.norm_apply_le_norm x))

/-- Evaluation on a constant-valued measurable indicator. -/
theorem complexIntegral_indicatorConst (μ : ComplexMeasure X)
    (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (c : ℂ) :
    complexIntegral μ (BoundedMeasurableFunction.indicatorConst s hs c) = c * μ s := by
  simpa [complexIntegral, BoundedMeasurableFunction.indicatorConst_apply] using
    (MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.integral_indicator_const
      (μ := μ) (B := ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℂ) c hs)

/-- Evaluation on a measurable characteristic function. -/
theorem complexIntegral_indicator (μ : ComplexMeasure X) (s : Set X) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    complexIntegral μ (BoundedMeasurableFunction.indicator s hs) = μ s := by
  simpa [BoundedMeasurableFunction.indicator] using
    complexIntegral_indicatorConst μ s hs (1 : ℂ)

/-- The finite sum formula for a measurable simple function. -/
theorem complexIntegral_ofSimpleFunc (μ : ComplexMeasure X) (f : SimpleFunc X ℂ) :
    complexIntegral μ (BoundedMeasurableFunction.ofSimpleFunc f) =
      ∑ c ∈ f.range, c * μ (f ⁻¹' {c}) := by
  have hf : μ.Integrable (fun x ↦ f x) := by
    simpa only [BoundedMeasurableFunction.ofSimpleFunc_apply] using
      complexIntegral_integrable μ (BoundedMeasurableFunction.ofSimpleFunc f)
  change (∫ᵛ x, f x ∂[ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℂ; μ]) = _
  rw [MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.integral_eq_setToFun]
  simpa [BoundedMeasurableFunction.ofSimpleFunc_apply,
    transpose_eq_cbmApplyMeasure, cbmApplyMeasure_apply,
    ContinuousLinearMap.mul_apply'] using
    (setToFun_simpleFunc (dominatedFinMeasAdditive_cbmApplyMeasure μ
      (ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℂ)) f hf)

@[simp]
theorem complexIntegral_dirac (a : X) (z : ℂ) (φ : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) :
    complexIntegral (MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.dirac a z) φ = φ a * z := by
  simpa [complexIntegral] using
    (MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.integral_dirac'
      (B := ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℂ)
      (f := fun x ↦ φ x) φ.measurable.stronglyMeasurable)

/-- Pointwise equal bounded measurable functions have equal complex integrals. -/
theorem complexIntegral_congr_fun (μ : ComplexMeasure X)
    {φ ψ : BoundedMeasurableFunction X} (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) :
    complexIntegral μ φ = complexIntegral μ ψ := by
  apply MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.integral_congr_ae
  exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall h

/-- Almost-everywhere equal bounded measurable functions have equal complex integrals. -/
theorem complexIntegral_congr_ae (μ : ComplexMeasure X)
    {φ ψ : BoundedMeasurableFunction X} (h : (fun x ↦ φ x) =ᵐ[μ.variation] fun x ↦ ψ x) :
    complexIntegral μ φ = complexIntegral μ ψ :=
  MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.integral_congr_ae h

/-- For a fixed complex measure, integration is a continuous complex-linear functional on bounded
measurable functions. -/
noncomputable def complexIntegralCLM (μ : ComplexMeasure X) :
    BoundedMeasurableFunction X →L[ℂ] ℂ :=
  LinearMap.mkContinuous
    { toFun := complexIntegral μ
      map_add' := complexIntegral_add μ
      map_smul' := complexIntegral_smul μ }
    (μ.variation.real univ)
    (fun φ ↦ by
      simpa [mul_comm] using norm_complexIntegral_le μ φ)

@[simp]
theorem complexIntegralCLM_apply (μ : ComplexMeasure X) (φ : BoundedMeasurableFunction X) :
    complexIntegralCLM μ φ = complexIntegral μ φ :=
  rfl

end

end MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure

module

public import MathlibExt.MeasureTheory.Measure.RegularDominated
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Complex
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.Decomposition.JordanSub
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.Variation.SignedMeasure

/-!
# Vector measures with regular total variation

This file records regularity of the total variation as a proposition, rather than a global
instance, and proves its stability under the standard vector-measure operations.  It also relates
regular variation of signed measures to regularity of their Jordan parts and regular variation of
complex measures to that of their real and imaginary parts.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Set
open scoped ENNReal NNReal

namespace MeasureTheory

noncomputable section

universe u v

namespace VectorMeasure

variable {X : Type u} {V : Type v}
variable [TopologicalSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X]
variable [NormedAddCommGroup V]

/-- A vector measure has regular variation when its total-variation measure is regular. -/
def HasRegularVariation (μ : VectorMeasure X V) : Prop :=
  μ.variation.Regular

namespace HasRegularVariation

theorem zero : HasRegularVariation (0 : VectorMeasure X V) := by
  rw [HasRegularVariation, variation_zero]
  infer_instance

theorem neg {μ : VectorMeasure X V} (hμ : HasRegularVariation μ) :
    HasRegularVariation (-μ) := by
  rw [HasRegularVariation, variation_neg]
  exact hμ

theorem add [R1Space X] [BorelSpace X] {μ ν : VectorMeasure X V}
    (hμ : HasRegularVariation μ)
    (hν : HasRegularVariation ν) [IsFiniteMeasure μ.variation]
    [IsFiniteMeasure ν.variation] : HasRegularVariation (μ + ν) := by
  let : μ.variation.Regular := hμ
  let : ν.variation.Regular := hν
  let : (μ.variation + ν.variation).Regular :=
    Measure.Regular.add_of_finite μ.variation ν.variation
  exact Measure.Regular.of_le variation_add_le

theorem sub [R1Space X] [BorelSpace X] {μ ν : VectorMeasure X V}
    (hμ : HasRegularVariation μ)
    (hν : HasRegularVariation ν) [IsFiniteMeasure μ.variation]
    [IsFiniteMeasure ν.variation] : HasRegularVariation (μ - ν) := by
  let : μ.variation.Regular := hμ
  let : ν.variation.Regular := hν
  let : (μ.variation + ν.variation).Regular :=
    Measure.Regular.add_of_finite μ.variation ν.variation
  exact Measure.Regular.of_le variation_sub_le

theorem smul {𝕜 : Type*} [NormedField 𝕜] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V]
    {μ : VectorMeasure X V} (hμ : HasRegularVariation μ) (c : 𝕜) :
    HasRegularVariation (c • μ) := by
  let : μ.variation.Regular := hμ
  rw [HasRegularVariation, variation_smul]
  infer_instance

theorem finsetSum [R1Space X] [BorelSpace X] {ι : Type*}
    (s : Finset ι) (μ : ι → VectorMeasure X V)
    (hfinite : ∀ i ∈ s, IsFiniteMeasure (μ i).variation)
    (hμ : ∀ i ∈ s, HasRegularVariation (μ i)) :
    HasRegularVariation (∑ i ∈ s, μ i) := by
  classical
  have hregularFinite : ∀ t : Finset ι,
      (∀ i ∈ t, IsFiniteMeasure (μ i).variation) →
      (∀ i ∈ t, HasRegularVariation (μ i)) →
      (∑ i ∈ t, (μ i).variation).Regular ∧
        IsFiniteMeasure (∑ i ∈ t, (μ i).variation) := by
    intro t
    induction t using Finset.induction_on with
    | empty =>
        intro _ _
        simp only [Finset.sum_empty]
        constructor <;> infer_instance
    | @insert i t hit ih =>
        intro htfinite htregular
        let _ : IsFiniteMeasure (μ i).variation :=
          htfinite i (Finset.mem_insert_self i t)
        let _ : (μ i).variation.Regular :=
          htregular i (Finset.mem_insert_self i t)
        obtain ⟨htRegular, htFinite⟩ := ih
          (fun j hj ↦ htfinite j (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hj))
          (fun j hj ↦ htregular j (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hj))
        let _ : (∑ j ∈ t, (μ j).variation).Regular := htRegular
        let _ : IsFiniteMeasure (∑ j ∈ t, (μ j).variation) := htFinite
        rw [Finset.sum_insert hit]
        exact ⟨Measure.Regular.add_of_finite _ _, by infer_instance⟩
  obtain ⟨hregular, hfiniteSum⟩ := hregularFinite s hfinite hμ
  let _ : (∑ i ∈ s, (μ i).variation).Regular := hregular
  let _ : IsFiniteMeasure (∑ i ∈ s, (μ i).variation) := hfiniteSum
  exact Measure.Regular.of_le (variation_finsetSum_le s μ)

end HasRegularVariation
end VectorMeasure

namespace SignedMeasure

variable {X : Type u}
variable [TopologicalSpace X] [R1Space X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]

omit [TopologicalSpace X] [R1Space X] [BorelSpace X] in
private theorem isFiniteMeasure_variation (s : SignedMeasure X) :
    IsFiniteMeasure s.variation := by
  rw [← s.totalVariation_eq_variation]
  infer_instance

omit [R1Space X] [BorelSpace X] in
/-- Regularity of a signed measure's total variation is exactly regular variation in the generic
vector-measure sense. -/
theorem totalVariation_regular_iff_hasRegularVariation (s : SignedMeasure X) :
    s.totalVariation.Regular ↔ VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation s := by
  rw [VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation, s.totalVariation_eq_variation]

/-- A signed measure has regular variation exactly when both measures in its Jordan decomposition
are regular. -/
theorem hasRegularVariation_iff_jordanParts_regular (s : SignedMeasure X) :
    VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation s ↔
      s.toJordanDecomposition.posPart.Regular ∧
        s.toJordanDecomposition.negPart.Regular := by
  constructor
  · intro hs
    let : s.variation.Regular := hs
    let : IsFiniteMeasure s.variation := isFiniteMeasure_variation s
    have hpos : s.toJordanDecomposition.posPart ≤ s.variation := by
      rw [← s.totalVariation_eq_variation, totalVariation]
      exact Measure.le_add_right le_rfl
    have hneg : s.toJordanDecomposition.negPart ≤ s.variation := by
      rw [← s.totalVariation_eq_variation, totalVariation]
      exact Measure.le_add_left le_rfl
    exact ⟨Measure.Regular.of_le hpos, Measure.Regular.of_le hneg⟩
  · rintro ⟨hpos, hneg⟩
    let : s.toJordanDecomposition.posPart.Regular := hpos
    let : s.toJordanDecomposition.negPart.Regular := hneg
    have htotal : s.totalVariation.Regular := by
      rw [totalVariation]
      exact Measure.Regular.add_of_finite _ _
    rw [VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation, ← s.totalVariation_eq_variation]
    exact htotal

omit [R1Space X] [BorelSpace X] in
/-- A finite regular positive measure has regular variation when regarded as a signed measure. -/
theorem hasRegularVariation_toSignedMeasure (μ : Measure X) [μ.Regular] [IsFiniteMeasure μ] :
    VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation μ.toSignedMeasure := by
  rw [VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation, Measure.variation_toSignedMeasure]
  infer_instance

/-- The difference of finite regular positive measures has regular variation as a signed measure. -/
theorem hasRegularVariation_toSignedMeasure_sub (μ ν : Measure X)
    [μ.Regular] [ν.Regular] [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] :
    VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation (μ.toSignedMeasure - ν.toSignedMeasure) := by
  have hμ := hasRegularVariation_toSignedMeasure μ
  have hν := hasRegularVariation_toSignedMeasure ν
  let : IsFiniteMeasure μ.toSignedMeasure.variation :=
    isFiniteMeasure_variation μ.toSignedMeasure
  let : IsFiniteMeasure ν.toSignedMeasure.variation :=
    isFiniteMeasure_variation ν.toSignedMeasure
  exact hμ.sub hν

end SignedMeasure

namespace ComplexMeasure

variable {X : Type u}
variable [TopologicalSpace X] [R1Space X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]

omit [TopologicalSpace X] [R1Space X] [BorelSpace X] in
/-- Total variation of a complex measure is bounded by the sum of the variations of its real and
imaginary parts. -/
theorem variation_le_re_add_im (c : ComplexMeasure X) :
    c.variation ≤ c.re.variation + c.im.variation := by
  apply VectorMeasure.variation_le_of_forall_enorm_le
  intro s hs
  rw [Measure.add_apply c.re.variation c.im.variation s]
  calc
    ‖c s‖ₑ ≤ ‖c.re s‖ₑ + ‖c.im s‖ₑ := by
      simp only [ComplexMeasure.re_apply, ComplexMeasure.im_apply]
      rw [enorm_eq_nnnorm, enorm_eq_nnnorm, enorm_eq_nnnorm, ← ENNReal.coe_add,
        ENNReal.coe_le_coe]
      exact_mod_cast Complex.norm_le_abs_re_add_abs_im (c s)
    _ ≤ c.re.variation s + c.im.variation s :=
      add_le_add (VectorMeasure.enorm_measure_le_variation _ _)
        (VectorMeasure.enorm_measure_le_variation _ _)

omit [TopologicalSpace X] [R1Space X] [BorelSpace X] in
/-- The variation of the real part of a complex measure is bounded by its complex variation. -/
theorem variation_re_le (c : ComplexMeasure X) : c.re.variation ≤ c.variation := by
  apply VectorMeasure.variation_le_of_forall_enorm_le
  intro s hs
  calc
    ‖c.re s‖ₑ ≤ ‖c s‖ₑ := by
      simp only [ComplexMeasure.re_apply, enorm_eq_nnnorm]
      exact_mod_cast Complex.abs_re_le_norm (c s)
    _ ≤ c.variation s := VectorMeasure.enorm_measure_le_variation _ _

omit [TopologicalSpace X] [R1Space X] [BorelSpace X] in
/-- The variation of the imaginary part of a complex measure is bounded by its complex variation. -/
theorem variation_im_le (c : ComplexMeasure X) : c.im.variation ≤ c.variation := by
  apply VectorMeasure.variation_le_of_forall_enorm_le
  intro s hs
  calc
    ‖c.im s‖ₑ ≤ ‖c s‖ₑ := by
      simp only [ComplexMeasure.im_apply, enorm_eq_nnnorm]
      exact_mod_cast Complex.abs_im_le_norm (c s)
    _ ≤ c.variation s := VectorMeasure.enorm_measure_le_variation _ _

omit [TopologicalSpace X] [R1Space X] [BorelSpace X] in
/-- Complex measures have finite total variation. -/
theorem isFiniteMeasure_variation (c : ComplexMeasure X) : IsFiniteMeasure c.variation := by
  let : IsFiniteMeasure c.re.variation := SignedMeasure.isFiniteMeasure_variation c.re
  let : IsFiniteMeasure c.im.variation := SignedMeasure.isFiniteMeasure_variation c.im
  exact isFiniteMeasure_of_le (c.re.variation + c.im.variation) (variation_le_re_add_im c)

/-- A complex measure has regular variation exactly when its real and imaginary signed measures
do. -/
theorem hasRegularVariation_iff_re_im (c : ComplexMeasure X) :
    VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation c ↔
      VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation c.re ∧ VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation c.im := by
  constructor
  · intro hc
    let : c.variation.Regular := hc
    let : IsFiniteMeasure c.variation := isFiniteMeasure_variation c
    exact ⟨Measure.Regular.of_le (variation_re_le c),
      Measure.Regular.of_le (variation_im_le c)⟩
  · rintro ⟨hre, him⟩
    let : c.re.variation.Regular := hre
    let : c.im.variation.Regular := him
    let : IsFiniteMeasure c.re.variation := SignedMeasure.isFiniteMeasure_variation c.re
    let : IsFiniteMeasure c.im.variation := SignedMeasure.isFiniteMeasure_variation c.im
    let : (c.re.variation + c.im.variation).Regular :=
      Measure.Regular.add_of_finite _ _
    exact Measure.Regular.of_le (variation_le_re_add_im c)

/-- Combining signed measures with regular variation produces a complex measure with regular
variation. -/
theorem hasRegularVariation_toComplexMeasure {s t : SignedMeasure X}
    (hs : VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation s) (ht : VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation t) :
    VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation (s.toComplexMeasure t) := by
  rw [hasRegularVariation_iff_re_im]
  rw [SignedMeasure.re_toComplexMeasure, SignedMeasure.im_toComplexMeasure]
  exact ⟨hs, ht⟩

/-- Regular variation is preserved by addition of complex measures. -/
theorem HasRegularVariation.add {c d : ComplexMeasure X}
    (hc : VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation c) (hd : VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation d) :
    VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation (c + d) := by
  let : IsFiniteMeasure c.variation := isFiniteMeasure_variation c
  let : IsFiniteMeasure d.variation := isFiniteMeasure_variation d
  exact hc.add hd

/-- Regular variation is preserved by subtraction of complex measures. -/
theorem HasRegularVariation.sub {c d : ComplexMeasure X}
    (hc : VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation c) (hd : VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation d) :
    VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation (c - d) := by
  let : IsFiniteMeasure c.variation := isFiniteMeasure_variation c
  let : IsFiniteMeasure d.variation := isFiniteMeasure_variation d
  exact hc.sub hd

omit [R1Space X] [BorelSpace X] in
/-- Regular variation is preserved by negation of complex measures. -/
theorem HasRegularVariation.neg {c : ComplexMeasure X}
    (hc : VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation c) :
    VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation (-c) :=
  hc.neg

omit [R1Space X] [BorelSpace X] in
/-- Regular variation is preserved by complex scalar multiplication. -/
theorem HasRegularVariation.smul {c : ComplexMeasure X}
    (hc : VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation c) (z : ℂ) :
    VectorMeasure.HasRegularVariation (z • c) :=
  hc.smul z

end ComplexMeasure

end

module

public import MathlibExt.Topology.Algebra.Group.ProfiniteCosetSectionZorn
public import Mathlib.GroupTheory.QuotientGroup.Basic

/-!
# Continuous equivariant coordinates for closed profinite subgroups

A genuine continuous closed-coset section gives a continuous left
`H`-equivariant retraction `G → H`, normalized on `H`. No normality or
finite-index hypothesis is used. The coordinate is noncanonical; its
existence and normalization are proved from the actual quotient section.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section
set_option autoImplicit false

open QuotientGroup

universe g

namespace Subgroup

variable {G : Type g} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
variable [CompactSpace G] [T2Space G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G]

/-- Every closed subgroup of a profinite group has a continuous,
left-equivariant retraction, with no normality or index restriction. -/
theorem exists_continuous_equivariant_retraction
    (H : Subgroup G) [IsClosed (H : Set G)] :
    ∃ r : C(G, H), (∀ (h : H) (g : G), r ((h : G) * g) = h * r g) ∧
      (∀ h : H, r (h : G) = h) := by
  obtain ⟨s₀, hs₀⟩ := QuotientGroup.exists_continuous_section_of_closedSubgroup_le
    (⊥ : Subgroup G) H bot_le
  let e : (G ⧸ (⊥ : Subgroup G)) ≃ₜ G :=
    { toEquiv := QuotientGroup.quotientBot.toEquiv
      continuous_toFun := continuous_quot_lift _ continuous_id
      continuous_invFun := QuotientGroup.continuous_mk }
  let q : C(G, G ⧸ H) := ⟨QuotientGroup.mk, QuotientGroup.continuous_mk⟩
  let s : C(G ⧸ H, G) := (⟨e, e.continuous⟩ : C(G ⧸ (⊥ : Subgroup G), G)).comp s₀
  have he (a : G ⧸ (⊥ : Subgroup G)) :
      q (e a) = QuotientGroup.cosetProjection (bot_le : (⊥ : Subgroup G) ≤ H) a := by
    obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := QuotientGroup.mk_surjective a
    rfl
  have hs (a : G ⧸ H) : q (s a) = a := (he (s₀ a)).trans (hs₀ a)
  let right : C(G, H) :=
    ⟨fun g => ⟨(s (q g))⁻¹ * g, QuotientGroup.eq.mp (hs (q g))⟩,
      Continuous.subtype_mk
        ((s.continuous.comp q.continuous).inv.mul continuous_id) _⟩
  have hright (g : G) (h : H) : right (g * (h : G)) = right g * h := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    change (s (q (g * (h : G))))⁻¹ * (g * (h : G)) =
      ((s (q g))⁻¹ * g) * (h : G)
    have hq : q (g * (h : G)) = q g := QuotientGroup.mk_mul_of_mem g h.property
    rw [hq, mul_assoc]
  let left : C(G, H) :=
    ⟨fun g => (right g⁻¹)⁻¹, (right.continuous.comp continuous_inv).inv⟩
  have hleft (h : H) (g : G) : left ((h : G) * g) = h * left g := by
    change (right (((h : G) * g)⁻¹))⁻¹ = h * (right g⁻¹)⁻¹
    rw [mul_inv_rev]
    have hr := hright g⁻¹ h⁻¹
    change right (g⁻¹ * (h : G)⁻¹) = right g⁻¹ * h⁻¹ at hr
    rw [hr, mul_inv_rev, inv_inv]
  let r : C(G, H) :=
    ⟨fun g => left g * (left 1)⁻¹, left.continuous.mul_const _⟩
  have hr (h : H) (g : G) : r ((h : G) * g) = h * r g := by
    change left ((h : G) * g) * (left 1)⁻¹ = h * (left g * (left 1)⁻¹)
    rw [hleft, mul_assoc]
  refine ⟨r, hr, fun h => ?_⟩
  have h := hr h 1
  simpa only [mul_one, r, ContinuousMap.coe_mk, mul_inv_cancel, mul_one] using h

/-- A chosen actual continuous left-equivariant retraction of a closed
subgroup; the choice is made from the proved closed-coset section theorem. -/
def continuousEquivariantRetraction (H : Subgroup G) [IsClosed (H : Set G)] : C(G, H) :=
  (exists_continuous_equivariant_retraction H).choose

/-- The chosen coordinate is left-equivariant for every subgroup element. -/
theorem continuousEquivariantRetraction_equivariant
    (H : Subgroup G) [IsClosed (H : Set G)] (h : H) (g : G) :
    continuousEquivariantRetraction H ((h : G) * g) =
      h * continuousEquivariantRetraction H g :=
  (exists_continuous_equivariant_retraction H).choose_spec.1 h g

/-- The chosen coordinate fixes every actual element of the closed subgroup. -/
theorem continuousEquivariantRetraction_subtype
    (H : Subgroup G) [IsClosed (H : Set G)] (h : H) :
    continuousEquivariantRetraction H (h : G) = h :=
  (exists_continuous_equivariant_retraction H).choose_spec.2 h

/-- The normalization fixes the identity element. -/
theorem continuousEquivariantRetraction_one
    (H : Subgroup G) [IsClosed (H : Set G)] :
    continuousEquivariantRetraction H (1 : G) = 1 :=
  continuousEquivariantRetraction_subtype H 1

end Subgroup

/-!
# The literal difference-coordinate shear

The original product coordinates transform by `(s,t) ↦ (s*t⁻¹,t)`, with
inverse `(r,t) ↦ (r*t,t)`. This is an actual homeomorphism of the original
topological product. Its inverse gives the literal linear pullback on
compact-support vector functions.

This geometric construction asserts no measure preservation or L2 norm
identity. Those are distinct prerequisites for its Hilbert-space unitary.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open scoped CompactlySupported

universe uG uH

namespace Homeomorph

/-- The actual difference-coordinate shear on the original product topological group. -/
def diagonalDifferenceShear (G : Type uG) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] : (G × G) ≃ₜ (G × G) where
  toFun z := (z.1 * z.2⁻¹, z.2)
  invFun z := (z.1 * z.2, z.2)
  left_inv z := by
    apply Prod.ext
    · change (z.1 * z.2⁻¹) * z.2 = z.1
      rw [mul_assoc, inv_mul_cancel, mul_one]
    · rfl
  right_inv z := by
    apply Prod.ext
    · change (z.1 * z.2) * z.2⁻¹ = z.1
      rw [mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel, mul_one]
    · rfl
  continuous_toFun := (continuous_fst.mul continuous_snd.inv).prodMk continuous_snd
  continuous_invFun := (continuous_fst.mul continuous_snd).prodMk continuous_snd

/-- The forward shear has its literal original difference-coordinate values. -/
@[simp]
theorem diagonalDifferenceShear_apply (G : Type uG) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] (z : G × G) :
    diagonalDifferenceShear G z = (z.1 * z.2⁻¹, z.2) :=
  rfl

/-- The inverse shear has its literal original multiplication-coordinate values. -/
@[simp]
theorem diagonalDifferenceShear_symm_apply (G : Type uG) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] (z : G × G) :
    (diagonalDifferenceShear G).symm z = (z.1 * z.2, z.2) :=
  rfl

end Homeomorph

namespace CompactlySupportedContinuousMap

variable {G : Type uG} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
variable {H : Type uH} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [NormedSpace ℂ H]

/-- The actual inverse-shear pullback on the original compact-support vector functions. -/
def diagonalShearPullback : C_c(G × G, H) →ₗ[ℂ] C_c(G × G, H) where
  toFun f :=
    ⟨⟨fun z => f ((Homeomorph.diagonalDifferenceShear G).symm z),
      f.continuous.comp (Homeomorph.diagonalDifferenceShear G).symm.continuous⟩,
      f.hasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph (Homeomorph.diagonalDifferenceShear G).symm⟩
  map_add' f g := by
    apply CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.ext
    intro z
    rfl
  map_smul' c f := by
    apply CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.ext
    intro z
    rfl

/-- The compact-support pullback retains the exact original inverse-shear vector coordinates. -/
@[simp]
theorem diagonalShearPullback_apply (f : C_c(G × G, H)) (z : G × G) :
    diagonalShearPullback f z = f (z.1 * z.2, z.2) :=
  rfl

end CompactlySupportedContinuousMap

/-!
# Normality of the identity component

The connected component of the identity in a topological group is a normal
subgroup.  This file packages the existing continuity and connected-component
APIs as a theorem, without registering a new global instance.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Subgroup

universe u

/-- The connected component of the identity is normal in every topological
group.  This is a theorem rather than a global instance, so consumers may
activate it only for the subgroup they own. -/
theorem connectedComponentOfOne_normal
    (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] :
    (connectedComponentOfOne G).Normal := by
  constructor
  intro n hn g
  change g * n * g⁻¹ ∈ connectedComponent (1 : G)
  have hn' : n ∈ connectedComponent (1 : G) := hn
  have hconj :
      g * n * g⁻¹ ∈ connectedComponent (g * (1 : G) * g⁻¹) :=
    (IsTopologicalGroup.continuous_conj g).mapsTo_connectedComponent
      (1 : G) hn'
  have hfix : g * (1 : G) * g⁻¹ = 1 := by
    simp
  simpa only [hfix] using hconj

end Subgroup

/-!
# Continuous maps and products of finite general linear groups

Continuous coefficient homomorphisms induce continuous entrywise maps on
finite general linear groups.  Finite general linear groups over a product
semiring are continuously multiplicatively equivalent to the product of the
two finite general linear groups.

The coefficient semirings and matrix index may live in independent universes.
Neither result requires commutativity or continuity of the semiring
operations.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup

universe uI uR uS

variable {ι : Type uI} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
variable {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS}
variable [Semiring R] [Semiring S]
variable [TopologicalSpace R] [TopologicalSpace S]
variable {f : R →+* S}

/-- A continuous coefficient homomorphism induces a continuous map on finite
general linear groups. The coefficient semirings and matrix index may live in
independent universes. -/
@[fun_prop]
theorem _root_.Continuous.generalLinearGroup_mapRingHom
    (hf : Continuous f) :
    Continuous (mapRingHom (n := ι) f) := by
  have hmatrix : Continuous (f.mapMatrix (m := ι)) := by
    change Continuous fun M : Matrix ι ι R => M.map f
    exact continuous_id.matrix_map hf
  change Continuous (Units.map (f.mapMatrix (m := ι)).toMonoidHom)
  exact Continuous.units_map _ hmatrix

/-- The algebraic product equivalence on finite general linear groups is a
homeomorphism in both directions for the finite matrix product topologies. -/
def prodContinuousMulEquiv :
    GL ι (R × S) ≃ₜ* GL ι R × GL ι S := by
  let matrixEquiv :
      Matrix ι ι (R × S) ≃ₜ* Matrix ι ι R × Matrix ι ι S :=
    { __ := (Matrix.prodRingEquiv (R := R) (S := S) ι).toMulEquiv
      continuous_toFun := by
        change Continuous fun M : Matrix ι ι (R × S) =>
          (M.map (RingHom.fst R S), M.map (RingHom.snd R S))
        exact (continuous_id.matrix_map continuous_fst).prodMk
          (continuous_id.matrix_map continuous_snd)
      continuous_invFun := by
        change Continuous fun p : Matrix ι ι R × Matrix ι ι S =>
          (fun i j => (p.1 i j, p.2 i j))
        refine continuous_matrix fun i j => ?_
        exact ((continuous_apply_apply i j).comp continuous_fst).prodMk
          ((continuous_apply_apply i j).comp continuous_snd) }
  let productUnitsEquiv :
      (Matrix ι ι R × Matrix ι ι S)ˣ ≃ₜ* GL ι R × GL ι S :=
    { __ := MulEquiv.prodUnits
      continuous_toFun :=
        (Homeomorph.prodUnits
          (α := Matrix ι ι R) (β := Matrix ι ι S)).continuous
      continuous_invFun :=
        (Homeomorph.prodUnits
          (α := Matrix ι ι R) (β := Matrix ι ι S)).symm.continuous }
  exact (Units.mapContinuousMulEquiv matrixEquiv).trans productUnitsEquiv
end Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup

  simp [scalarMatrixPath, Matrix.scalar_apply]

private theorem scalarMatrixPath_one
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [Module ℝ R] :
    scalarMatrixPath (I := I) (R := R) 1 = 1 := by
  ext i j
  simp [scalarMatrixPath, Matrix.scalar_apply]

private theorem continuous_scalarMatrixPath
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    [Module ℝ R] [ContinuousSMul ℝ R] :
    Continuous (scalarMatrixPath (I := I) (R := R)) := by
  refine continuous_matrix fun i j => ?_
  simp only [scalarMatrixPath, Matrix.scalar_apply, Matrix.diagonal_apply]
  split_ifs <;> fun_prop

private def scaledMatrixPath
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [Module ℝ R]
    (q : GL I R) (t : unitInterval) : Matrix I I R :=
  scalarMatrixPath (I := I) t * (q : Matrix I I R)

private theorem continuous_scaledMatrixPath
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    [IsTopologicalRing R] [Module ℝ R] [ContinuousSMul ℝ R]
    (q : GL I R) : Continuous (scaledMatrixPath q) := by
  exact (continuous_scalarMatrixPath (I := I) (R := R)).matrix_mul
    continuous_const

private theorem scaledMatrixPath_zero
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [Module ℝ R] (q : GL I R) :
    scaledMatrixPath q 0 = 0 := by
  simp [scaledMatrixPath, scalarMatrixPath_zero]

private theorem scaledMatrixPath_one
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [Module ℝ R] (q : GL I R) :
    scaledMatrixPath q 1 = (q : Matrix I I R) := by
  simp [scaledMatrixPath, scalarMatrixPath_one]

private def whiteheadTriple
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [Module ℝ R]
    (q : GL I R) (t : unitInterval) : GL (I ⊕ I) R :=
  BlockElementary.upperUnit (scaledMatrixPath q t) *
    (BlockElementary.lowerUnit (scaledMatrixPath q⁻¹ t))⁻¹ *
    BlockElementary.upperUnit (scaledMatrixPath q t)

private theorem continuous_whiteheadTriple
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    [IsTopologicalRing R] [Module ℝ R] [ContinuousSMul ℝ R]
    (q : GL I R) : Continuous (whiteheadTriple q) := by
  exact ((continuous_upperUnit _ (continuous_scaledMatrixPath q)).mul
    (continuous_inv.comp
      (continuous_lowerUnit _ (continuous_scaledMatrixPath q⁻¹)))).mul
    (continuous_upperUnit _ (continuous_scaledMatrixPath q))

private theorem whiteheadTriple_zero
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [Module ℝ R] (q : GL I R) :
    whiteheadTriple q 0 = 1 := by
  simp [whiteheadTriple, scaledMatrixPath_zero,
    BlockElementary.upperUnit_zero, BlockElementary.lowerUnit_zero]

private theorem whiteheadTriple_one
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [Module ℝ R] (q : GL I R) :
    whiteheadTriple q 1 =
      BlockElementary.upperUnit (q : Matrix I I R) *
        BlockElementary.lowerUnit (-(↑(q⁻¹) : Matrix I I R)) *
        BlockElementary.upperUnit (q : Matrix I I R) := by
  simp only [whiteheadTriple, scaledMatrixPath_one, lowerUnit_inv]

private theorem whiteheadTriple_one_inv
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [Module ℝ R] :
    (whiteheadTriple (1 : GL I R) 1)⁻¹ =
      BlockElementary.upperUnit (-1 : Matrix I I R) *
        BlockElementary.lowerUnit (1 : Matrix I I R) *
        BlockElementary.upperUnit (-1 : Matrix I I R) := by
  rw [whiteheadTriple_one]
  simp only [inv_one, Units.val_one]
  let U : GL (I ⊕ I) R := BlockElementary.upperUnit (1 : Matrix I I R)
  let L : GL (I ⊕ I) R := BlockElementary.lowerUnit (-1 : Matrix I I R)
  have hfirst : (U * L * U)⁻¹ = U⁻¹ * (U * L)⁻¹ :=
    _root_.mul_inv_rev (U * L) U
  have hsecond : (U * L)⁻¹ = L⁻¹ * U⁻¹ := _root_.mul_inv_rev U L
  change (U * L * U)⁻¹ = _
  rw [hfirst, hsecond]
  dsimp only [U, L]
  simp only [upperUnit_inv, lowerUnit_inv, neg_neg, mul_assoc]

private def whiteheadKernelPath
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [Module ℝ R]
    (q : GL I R) (t : unitInterval) : GL (I ⊕ I) R :=
  whiteheadTriple q t * (whiteheadTriple (1 : GL I R) t)⁻¹

private theorem continuous_whiteheadKernelPath
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    [IsTopologicalRing R] [Module ℝ R] [ContinuousSMul ℝ R]
    (q : GL I R) : Continuous (whiteheadKernelPath q) := by
  exact (continuous_whiteheadTriple q).mul
    (continuous_inv.comp (continuous_whiteheadTriple (1 : GL I R)))

private theorem whiteheadKernelPath_zero
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [Module ℝ R] (q : GL I R) :
    whiteheadKernelPath q 0 = 1 := by
  simp [whiteheadKernelPath, whiteheadTriple_zero]

private theorem whiteheadKernelPath_one
    {R : Type uR} [Ring R] [Module ℝ R] (q : GL I R) :
    whiteheadKernelPath q 1 = diagUnit q := by
  rw [whiteheadKernelPath, whiteheadTriple_one,
    whiteheadTriple_one_inv]
  simpa only [mul_assoc] using diagUnit_eq_six_unipotent q

private theorem scaledMatrixPath_map_eq_one
    {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} [Ring R] [Semiring S]
    [Module ℝ R] (σ : R →+* S) (q : GL I R)
    (hq : mapRingHom σ q = 1) (t : unitInterval) :
    (scaledMatrixPath q t).map σ =
      (scaledMatrixPath (1 : GL I R) t).map σ := by
  have hqval := congrArg Units.val hq
  change (q : Matrix I I R).map σ = 1 at hqval
  simp only [scaledMatrixPath, Matrix.map_mul, hqval,
    Units.val_one, Matrix.mul_one]

private theorem map_whiteheadTriple_eq_one
    {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} [Ring R] [Semiring S]
    [Module ℝ R] (σ : R →+* S) (q : GL I R)
    (hq : mapRingHom σ q = 1) (t : unitInterval) :
    mapRingHom σ (whiteheadTriple q t) =
      mapRingHom σ (whiteheadTriple (1 : GL I R) t) := by
  have hqinv : mapRingHom σ q⁻¹ = 1 := by
    rw [map_inv, hq, inv_one]
  have hscaled := scaledMatrixPath_map_eq_one σ q hq t
  have hscaledInv := scaledMatrixPath_map_eq_one σ q⁻¹ hqinv t
  simp only [whiteheadTriple, map_mul, map_inv]
  rw [map_upperUnit_eq_of_map_eq σ _ _ hscaled,
    map_lowerUnit_eq_of_map_eq σ _ _ hscaledInv]
  simp only [inv_one]

private theorem map_whiteheadKernelPath
    {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} [Ring R] [Semiring S]
    [Module ℝ R] (σ : R →+* S) (q : GL I R)
    (hq : mapRingHom σ q = 1) (t : unitInterval) :
    mapRingHom σ (whiteheadKernelPath q t) = 1 := by
  rw [whiteheadKernelPath, map_mul, map_inv,
    map_whiteheadTriple_eq_one σ q hq t]
  exact mul_inv_cancel _

private def whiteheadKernelCurve
    {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} [Ring R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    [IsTopologicalRing R] [Module ℝ R] [ContinuousSMul ℝ R]
    [Semiring S] (σ : R →+* S)
    (q : (mapRingHom (n := I) σ).ker) :
    C(unitInterval, (mapRingHom (n := I ⊕ I) σ).ker) :=
  ⟨fun t => ⟨whiteheadKernelPath q.1 t,
      MonoidHom.mem_ker.mpr
        (map_whiteheadKernelPath σ q.1
          (MonoidHom.mem_ker.mp q.property) t)⟩,
    (continuous_whiteheadKernelPath q.1).subtype_mk _⟩

private theorem whiteheadKernelCurve_zero
    {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} [Ring R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    [IsTopologicalRing R] [Module ℝ R] [ContinuousSMul ℝ R]
    [Semiring S] (σ : R →+* S)
    (q : (mapRingHom (n := I) σ).ker) :
    whiteheadKernelCurve σ q 0 = 1 := by
  apply Subtype.ext
  exact whiteheadKernelPath_zero q.1

private theorem whiteheadKernelCurve_one
    {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} [Ring R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    [IsTopologicalRing R] [Module ℝ R] [ContinuousSMul ℝ R]
    [Semiring S] (σ : R →+* S)
    (q : (mapRingHom (n := I) σ).ker) :
    (whiteheadKernelCurve σ q 1).1 = diagUnit q.1 := by
  exact whiteheadKernelPath_one q.1

open scoped commutatorElement

/-- A padded commutator in a finite coefficient kernel belongs to the
identity component of the doubled coefficient kernel. -/
theorem paddedCommutator_mem_connectedComponent_ker
    {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} [Ring R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    [IsTopologicalRing R] [Module ℝ R] [ContinuousSMul ℝ R]
    [Semiring S] (σ : R →+* S)
    (g h : (mapRingHom (n := I) σ).ker) :
    ∃ z : (mapRingHom (n := I ⊕ I) σ).ker,
      z.1 = blockDiagonalOne I I R ⁅g.1, h.1⁆ ∧
        z ∈ connectedComponent
          (1 : (mapRingHom (n := I ⊕ I) σ).ker) := by
  let q : (mapRingHom (n := I) σ).ker := g⁻¹ * h⁻¹
  let Pg := whiteheadKernelCurve σ g
  let Ph := whiteheadKernelCurve σ h
  let Pq := whiteheadKernelCurve σ q
  let P : C(unitInterval, (mapRingHom (n := I ⊕ I) σ).ker) :=
    Pg * Ph * Pq
  have hP0 : P 0 = 1 := by
    simp only [P, Pg, Ph, Pq, ContinuousMap.mul_apply,
      whiteheadKernelCurve_zero, mul_one]
  have hP1 : (P 1).1 = blockDiagonalOne I I R ⁅g.1, h.1⁆ := by
    change (whiteheadKernelCurve σ g 1).1 *
        (whiteheadKernelCurve σ h 1).1 *
          (whiteheadKernelCurve σ q 1).1 = _
    rw [whiteheadKernelCurve_one, whiteheadKernelCurve_one,
      whiteheadKernelCurve_one]
    exact diagUnit_commutator_eq g.1 h.1
  have hjoined : Joined
      (1 : (mapRingHom (n := I ⊕ I) σ).ker) (P 1) :=
    ⟨Path.mk P hP0 rfl⟩
  refine ⟨P 1, hP1, ?_⟩
  exact pathComponent_subset_component
    (1 : (mapRingHom (n := I ⊕ I) σ).ker) hjoined

end KernelPaddedCommutator

module

public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.ClopenNhdofOne
public import Mathlib.Topology.Separation.Connected
public import Mathlib.Topology.Separation.Regular
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Filtered.Final
public import MathlibExt.Topology.Algebra.Group.OpenNormalComap
public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Group.Subgroup

/-!
# Ambient open normal subgroups below an open subgroup

For an open subgroup `H` of a profinite group `G`, ambient open normal
subgroups contained in `H` form a nonempty inf-semilattice.  Its opposite is
therefore filtered.  This is the cofinal index shape on which finite-quotient
corestriction has constant subgroup index.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open CategoryTheory

namespace OpenSubgroup

universe u

instance {G : Type u} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
    (H : OpenSubgroup G) : IsTopologicalGroup H :=
  inferInstanceAs (IsTopologicalGroup H.toSubgroup)

instance {G : Type u} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
    [CompactSpace G] (H : OpenSubgroup G) : CompactSpace H :=
  isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mp H.isClosed.isCompact

end OpenSubgroup

namespace OpenNormalSubgroup

universe u

variable {G : Type u} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]

/-- An ambient open normal subgroup of `G` contained in the supplied open
subgroup. -/
structure BelowOpen (H : OpenSubgroup G) where
  /-- The ambient open normal subgroup. -/
  obj : OpenNormalSubgroup G
  /-- Containment in the open subgroup. -/
  le_open : obj.toSubgroup ≤ H.toSubgroup

namespace BelowOpen

variable {H : OpenSubgroup G}

/-- Forget containment and retain the ambient open normal subgroup. -/
def objEmbedding : BelowOpen H ↪ OpenNormalSubgroup G where
  toFun := BelowOpen.obj
  inj' := by
    rintro ⟨U, hU⟩ ⟨V, hV⟩ h
    cases h
    rfl

instance : PartialOrder (BelowOpen H) :=
  PartialOrder.lift BelowOpen.obj objEmbedding.injective

@[simp]
theorem le_iff (U V : BelowOpen H) : U ≤ V ↔ U.obj ≤ V.obj :=
  Iff.rfl

instance : Min (BelowOpen H) where
  min U V :=
    ⟨U.obj ⊓ V.obj, fun _g hg => U.le_open ((inf_le_left : U.obj ⊓ V.obj ≤ U.obj) hg)⟩

@[simp]
theorem obj_inf (U V : BelowOpen H) : (U ⊓ V).obj = U.obj ⊓ V.obj :=
  rfl

instance : SemilatticeInf (BelowOpen H) where
  inf := fun U V => U ⊓ V
  inf_le_left U V := by
    exact (show U.obj ⊓ V.obj ≤ U.obj from inf_le_left)
  inf_le_right U V := by
    exact (show U.obj ⊓ V.obj ≤ V.obj from inf_le_right)
  le_inf U V W hUV hUW := by
    exact (show U.obj ≤ V.obj ⊓ W.obj from le_inf hUV hUW)

section Profinite

variable [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G]
variable [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G]

instance : Nonempty (BelowOpen H) := by
  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ :=
    ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one H.isOpen H.one_mem
  exact ⟨⟨U, hU⟩⟩

/-- The opposite containment poset of ambient open normal subgroups below
an open subgroup is filtered. -/
instance : IsFiltered (BelowOpen H)ᵒᵖ := inferInstance

end Profinite

/-- Inclusion of the bounded ambient open-normal poset into all ambient
open normal subgroups. -/
def inclusion : BelowOpen H ⥤ OpenNormalSubgroup G where
  obj U := U.obj
  map {U V} f := homOfLE (show U.obj ≤ V.obj from leOfHom f)
  map_id _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  map_comp _ _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- Preimage functor from the bounded ambient index to the full subgroup
open-normal index. -/
def comapFunctor (H : OpenSubgroup G) :
    (BelowOpen H)ᵒᵖ ⥤ (OpenNormalSubgroup H)ᵒᵖ where
  obj U := Opposite.op
    (OpenNormalSubgroup.comap
      (ContinuousMonoidHom.mk H.toSubgroup.subtype continuous_subtype_val)
      U.unop.obj)
  map {_U _V} f :=
    (homOfLE (OpenNormalSubgroup.comap_mono
      (ContinuousMonoidHom.mk H.toSubgroup.subtype continuous_subtype_val)
      (leOfHom f.unop))).op
  map_id _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  map_comp _ _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _

section Final

variable [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G]
variable [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G]

/-- Restricting the ambient open-normal system to subgroups contained in a
fixed open subgroup is final after passing to reverse inclusion. -/
instance (H : OpenSubgroup G) :
    ((inclusion (H := H)).op).Final := by
  apply Functor.final_of_exists_of_isFiltered
  · intro U
    let W : BelowOpen H := Classical.choice inferInstance
    let V : BelowOpen H :=
      ⟨U.unop ⊓ W.obj, fun _g hg => W.le_open
        ((inf_le_right : U.unop ⊓ W.obj ≤ W.obj) hg)⟩
    exact ⟨Opposite.op V,
      ⟨(homOfLE (show V.obj ≤ U.unop from inf_le_left)).op⟩⟩
  · intro _ c _ _
    exact ⟨c, 𝟙 _, by subsingleton⟩

/-- The bounded ambient preimage functor is final: every subgroup
open-normal stage is refined by one coming from an ambient open normal
subgroup contained in `H`. -/
instance (H : OpenSubgroup G) : (comapFunctor H).Final := by
  apply Functor.final_of_exists_of_isFiltered
  · intro V
    let S : Subgroup G := V.unop.toSubgroup.map H.toSubgroup.subtype
    have hSopen : IsOpen (S : Set G) := by
      change IsOpen (H.toSubgroup.subtype '' (V.unop : Set H))
      exact H.isOpen.isOpenMap_subtype_val _ V.unop.isOpen
    obtain ⟨U, hUV⟩ :=
      ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one hSopen S.one_mem
    have hUH : U.toSubgroup ≤ H.toSubgroup := by
      refine hUV.trans ?_
      intro g hg
      rcases hg with ⟨v, _hv, rfl⟩
      exact v.property
    let U' : BelowOpen H := ⟨U, hUH⟩
    have hcomap : OpenNormalSubgroup.comap
        (ContinuousMonoidHom.mk H.toSubgroup.subtype continuous_subtype_val)
        U ≤ V.unop := by
      intro h hh
      change h ∈ V.unop
      rcases hUV hh with ⟨v, hv, heq⟩
      have heq' : (v : H) = h := by
        apply Subtype.ext
        exact heq
      exact heq' ▸ hv
    exact ⟨Opposite.op U', ⟨(homOfLE hcomap).op⟩⟩
  · intro _ c _ _
    exact ⟨c, 𝟙 _, by subsingleton⟩

end Final

end BelowOpen

end OpenNormalSubgroup
